subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs gain a supported model/provider override contract, and if so should it reuse `payload.model`, use top-level job fields, or introduce a dedicated run-scoped `sessionOverride` block?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes public cron schema, provider/model precedence, session-state mutation, persistence, UI/CLI semantics, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Extend `systemEvent` with `payload.model`
options.body: Reuse the existing per-job model contract for the system-event branch, with strict validation and run-scoped application to the cron child session.

options.title: Add explicit job/session override fields
options.body: Introduce top-level `model`/`provider` or a `sessionOverride` block that can apply across payload kinds, accepting a broader protocol and docs surface.

options.title: Keep system events text-only
options.body: Document isolated `agentTurn` as the supported per-job model path and leave main-session system events tied to the target session's current model state.

recommendation.title: Extend `systemEvent` with `payload.model`
recommendation.body: Reuse the existing per-job model contract for the system-event branch, with strict validation and run-scoped application to the cron child session.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron runtime, session target, and model-routing history makes this the best available owner for the product/API choice.
